narrative.overview: The first screen is a single image: Nyala, the brand spirit, standing large and centred before an anime-style painted pine forest, with sunlight glowing through the treetops, floating sparkles of light and bright grass below. Nyala is the focal point; the forest is the world she stands in. Around her, the interface is quiet signage: thin moonlight type, a vertical wordmark, hairline corner brackets, and one small framed button. The mood is hushed and unhurried. There are no decorative props, glows or particle effects added by the interface; the painting supplies the light and mood, and Nyala supplies the focus. Type is light and sparse.
keyCharacteristics: An anime-style painted forest as the ground, lightly shaded at the top, sides and lower band, bright and glowing at the centre
Nyala large, sharp and centred, the only focal element
The Nyala Font, a hand-drawn storybook script, for the wordmark and headline; a light grotesk for everything else
Hairline corner brackets frame the reading zone
No props, glows or ambient animation in the hero

rules.name: The Painting Carries the Colour Rule
rules.body: Colour comes from the forest painting and from Nyala herself. The interface adds no accent colour, glow or tint.

rules.name: The No-Accent-Button Rule
rules.body: The primary action is a moonlight hairline frame on a dark frosted fill, not a coloured button.

rules.name: The Script Is a Voice Rule
rules.body: The Nyala Font sets only the wordmark and headlines; body copy, labels, buttons and numbers stay in Hanken Grotesk. One weight, no synthesised bold or light.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: No eyebrow or kicker labels above headings. The headline speaks for itself.

rules.name: The One Figure Rule
rules.body: Nyala is the only figure in the hero. Anything else belongs to the painting or the interface layer, never between.

dos: Do keep interface type in moonlight white, at weights 200–400.
Do keep the forest bright and glowing at the centre, behind Nyala; shade only where text sits.
Do shade the painting where type sits (top edge, sides, lower band) rather than boxing the type.
Do frame reading zones with hairline corner brackets rather than boxes or cards.
donts: Don't add props, glows, particles or ambient animation to the hero.
Don't use gradient text, kicker labels or coloured accent buttons in this world.
Don't place copy over Nyala; size her so she clears the headline.
Don't carry the legacy section styles (Plus Jakarta Sans headings, pill buttons, rounded cards, shimmer text) into new surfaces.
